name: varnic
author: playground (playground & kitchen-table games)
description: varnic (playground/kitchen-table direction). OBJECT: a finished, DRAWN Connect Four board, drawn as a framed 7-wide x 6-tall grid of R/Y counters. CLUE: '<row5> <row6> <k>' -- the two BOTTOM rows of the finished board (upper of the two first, i.e. exactly the last two lines of the picture) and a number k in 4..11. SOLUTION: the whole 6x7 board (any decoration; the scorer reads the R/Y characters in reading order and ignores everything else) such that (A) exactly 42 counters, (B) exactly 21 R and 21 Y -- they took turns, (C) its last two rows are exactly the clue's two rows, (D) NO four-in-a-row of one colour in any of the four directions -- nobody won, the board just filled up, and (E) THE HIDDEN MEASUREMENT: exactly k counters are hemmed in -- every counter orthogonally adjacent to them (up/down/left/right, board edges simply do not count) is the other colour. Equivalently 'counters with no touching friend', counting edge and corner counters too, which is the arbitrary-but-natural wrinkle. E is nameless; A-D are things a 12-year-old reads off one picture. Diagonal neighbours are NOT considered for E (decoy), and E is colour-blind (decoy: reds only / yellows only). INTENDED PATH: demo 1 -> 'that's Connect 4'; count discs (42), count colours (21/21), notice no four in a row, notice the clue's 14 letters are the bottom two rows; then the only question left is 'what does k count?', and the demos are (board, k) pairs to fit it against. WITNESSES CLOSED: no minimal/partial witness exists because the object is a fixed-size complete board (clause A); the empty string, the clue itself and any junk have != 42 R/Y chars; the clue's rows repeated or any solid block dies on (D); a board that satisfies A-D but not E is the blind-play answer and scores 0 -- measured blind hit rate 8.7% (a random A-D board has k counters hemmed in with that probability, averaged over the uniform k in 4..11), so a team without E is pinned near the 'failed' band while a team with E scores 100%. Cache-and-replay is closed by the clue space (about 9.4k valid two-row prefixes x 8 values of k). generate() rejects two-row prefixes with a four-run and ones where >3 bottom-row counters are already hemmed in by the clue alone (their status is fixed by the clue, so a small k would be infeasible); k in 4..11 keeps solve() at ~10ms typical / ~110ms worst. solve() is a seeded restart hill-climb over the 28 free cells with plateau moves and a 2% uphill kick; it never emits a canonical board -- the board is a fresh random draw per clue.
